correctness.rationale: With normalized counting measure, Schur orthogonality yields an orthonormal matrix-coefficient basis, and the transposition-character Gram is exactly (n-1)/n! times 2I+B^T B+(n-5)J. Full-class edge incidence has BB^T=(n-2)I+J and the explicit strictly positive spectrum for n>=4; every selected edge-set matrix is a positive principal submatrix. The n>=5 bottom eigenvalue uses positivity of B^TB+(n-5)J and the bipartite-component rank identity. For r-regular graphs, BB^T=rI+A, so the entire multiset, spectral inversion, and n>=6,r>=3 sharp conditioning follow algebraically. The skew-symmetric coefficient kernel has the same dimension as the full-class nullity. Finite exact checker output is a consistency check and is not used to infer universality.

value.rationale: Graph-indexed transposition evaluations are a canonical sparse sample pattern for the standard nonabelian Fourier block on S_n. The theorem establishes universal interpolation for all edge masks, classifies bottom singular-space degeneracy by bipartite components, identifies exactly the full-class hidden skew coefficient space, and for every fixed regular degree transfers the full graph adjacency spectrum into concentration eigenvalues with a topology-independent sharp condition number. These are natural whole-family structural and inverse-spectral statements, not a numerical table or arbitrary narrow parameter.
